newsitem.title: USA: Stokely says willing to listen to holder.
newsitem.headline: Stokely says willing to listen to holder.

text.p: Stokely USA Inc said Tuesday it would review details of a large shareholder's proposals if they were presented.

"If you provide us with some details, we'd be happy to review them and get back to you," Steve Theobald, Stokely president said he told Brad Richdale, a businessman who said he bought a nine percent stake in the producer of canned vegetables.
"He indicated that he would do that. Until then we are not in position to react. We don't know anything about his intentions," Theobald said in a telephone interview.
Yesterday, Florida-based, privately-held National Direct Corp, said that its founder, Richdale, had taken a nine percent interest in the company.
Richdale had said that he had met last week with Theobald and suggested ways for the company, which has lost money in four of its last five fiscal years, to become profitable again.

Richdale, in a news release, said Stokely should create new proprietary signature products with higher margins and develop new health-and-fitness-related products that could be sold though a direct sales force.
"I'm hopeful the board will see the wisdom of my marketing ideas developed from two decades of experience in the field," said Richdale.
National Direct Corp is a marketing company that claims $80 million in annual revenues.

Wisconsin-based Stokely reported a loss for its fiscal year ended March 31, 1997 of $7.4 million or a loss of $0.65 a share before restructuring and other charges. Sales fell to $206.3 million from $184.9 million in fiscal 1996.
Shares of Stokely closed up 1/16 to two on turnover of more than 117,000 shares.
